product.name: Chat Pro Repository MCP
product.purpose: Give ChatGPT bounded local repository development and an exact task-bound GitHub lifecycle while preserving server-side policy, durable recovery, and owner-only merge approval.

primary_users.role: Solo developer or small-team technical owner
primary_users.technical_level: Comfortable with code and Git but unwilling to grant a model arbitrary machine or GitHub authority.
primary_users.work_context: Uses ChatGPT to understand, change, validate, review, and carry an isolated repository task through Draft pull request, CI, review, and one exact approved merge.

primary_users.role: Developer operating ChatGPT or a separate implementation worker
primary_users.technical_level: Able to inspect repository and lifecycle evidence and expects stale state and partial effects to fail safely.
primary_users.work_context: Coordinates local implementation, external-worker evidence, GitHub review, CI, and recovery while the MCP server enforces repository and task boundaries.

jobs_to_be_done.statement: Understand product intent, architecture, code, and current Git state through bounded reads.
Make coherent policy-checked local changes directly or through bounded external-worker artifacts without granting provider or machine authority.
Validate and review actual repository bytes, Git objects, scope, CI, and review evidence rather than trusting a claimed result.
Open and operate an exact task worktree, push its fixed branch, maintain a Draft pull request, handle CI and review, obtain one exact owner merge approval, and recover without blind replay.
Recover across crashes and sessions without replaying uncertain effects or losing task and artifact evidence.

must_reduce: Repeated reconstruction of repository and product context
Blind replay after interrupted external effects
Unreviewed push, pull-request, CI, review, or merge actions
Context loss between ChatGPT, external workers, local Git, and GitHub
must_not_become: A generic shell, Git command runner, or GitHub API proxy
A tool for adding repository roots or reading credentials
A release, deployment, signing, publication, or infrastructure service
experience_principles: Actual bytes and Git objects before claims
Deterministic validation and review before external mutation
One exact owner decision for one exact merge
Optional specialist workflows rather than mandatory ceremony
